**Step 1: Convert the time worked into hours.**
We know that there are 60 minutes in 1 hour.
Weng worked 50 minutes.
$$ \text{Hours} = \frac{50 \text{ minutes}}{60 \text{ minutes/hour}} $$
Simplifying the fraction:
$$ \text{Hours} = \frac{5}{6} \text{ hours} $$

**Step 2: Calculate the earnings.**
Her hourly wage is $12.
$$ \text{Earnings} = \text{Hourly Wage} \times \text{Hours Worked} $$
$$ \text{Earnings} = 12 \times \frac{5}{6} $$

$$ \text{Earnings} = \frac{12 \times 5}{6} = \frac{60}{6} = 10 $$
